answer_text:
Let

\[
\alpha=\sqrt[80]{43},\qquad \beta=\sqrt[84]{43}
\]

with the usual convention that these are the positive real roots. We want

\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta):\mathbb{Q}].
\]

Set

\[
\gamma=\frac{\alpha}{\beta}\in \mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta).
\]

Now compute a power of \(\gamma\). Since

\[
\operatorname{lcm}(80,84)=1680,
\]

we have

\[
\gamma^{1680}
=\left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta}\right)^{1680}
=\frac{\alpha^{1680}}{\beta^{1680}}
=\frac{(\alpha^{80})^{21}}{(\beta^{84})^{20}}
=\frac{43^{21}}{43^{20}}
=43.
\]

Thus \(\gamma\) is a \(1680\)th root of \(43\). Because \(\alpha,\beta>0\), \(\gamma>0\), so

\[
\gamma=\sqrt[1680]{43}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\alpha=\sqrt[80]{43}
=\left(43^{1/1680}\right)^{21}
=\gamma^{21},
\]

and similarly

\[
\beta=\sqrt[84]{43}
=\left(43^{1/1680}\right)^{20}
=\gamma^{20}.
\]

Hence

\[
\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta)\subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\gamma).
\]

Conversely, since \(\gamma=\alpha/\beta\),

\[
\mathbb{Q}(\gamma)\subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta).
\]

So

\[
\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta)=\mathbb{Q}(\gamma).
\]

Now consider the polynomial

\[
f(x)=x^{1680}-43.
\]

It is irreducible over \(\mathbb{Q}\) by Eisenstein’s criterion at the prime \(43\): every non-leading coefficient except the constant term is \(0\), and the constant term is divisible by \(43\) but not by \(43^2\).

Since \(\gamma\) is a root of this irreducible polynomial,

\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\gamma):\mathbb{Q}]=1680.
\]

Therefore

\[
[\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[80]{43},\sqrt[84]{43}):\mathbb{Q}]
=
[\mathbb{Q}(\gamma):\mathbb{Q}]
=
1680.
\]

\[
\boxed{1680}
\]
